newsitem.title: UK: London gold stalls while palladium shines.
newsitem.headline: London gold stalls while palladium shines.

text.p: Gold prices wallowed in a narrow price range on Tuesday, failing to excite enough interest in the market to carry through an upside push.
The only real mover among the precious metals was palladium, which popped higher in the afternoon to fix a $128.00 an ounce, up $2.25 from the morning and the highest in nearly six months.
The early market buzz favoured a foray by gold towards the psychological $350 an ounce level, as the market is technically oversold.
"New York tried to push it up to $347 a couple of times, but it came right back down again. I think the market was just fed up with it," a dealer said.
"It had to break $347 to get anywhere higher, but it just looks so unattractive," he added.
Bullion fixed at $345.70 an ounce, compared to $346.30 in the morning. Values were up about $2.00 from the fixing on Monday afternoon but little changed from firmer London closing levels.
Even if gold managed to break higher later in the week, gold's steep downtrend was still in effect and gains would be shortlived, analysts said.
Prices, already at 3-1/4 year lows, had briefly pushed just below an important 12-year support line last week. That left gold vulnerable to more losses.
"I suspect we'll see the market try to regain $350, fail miserably and come lower," said analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston.
Recent lows around $343.50 would cushion a decline, but $340 was the critical support level.
The market was expecting little direction from the U.S. Federal Reserve's two day meeting, which starts on Tuesday. Analysts expected the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged amid tame inflation.
"The feeling is there won't be any surprises. They're not likely to change interest rates which means little effect on the market," a dealer said.
Silver was little changed from Monday's London close, down one cent at $4.89/$4.91 an ounce, while platinum at $352.45/$353.45 was $1.45 firmer.
Palladium, last quoted at $127.75/$128.75, has moved steadily higher in recent months due to continued delays in the 1997 export contract talks between Japan and Russia for platinum group metals.
